chunks: Ahmad ibn Idris and others, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ali ibn al-Rayyan, from his father, from Yunus or others, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you, it reached me that you used to do something regarding the produce of Ayn Ziyad, and I love to hear it from you.' So he said to me, 'Yes. I used to order that when the fruit ripened, grooves be made in its walls so that people could enter and eat. And I used to order that every day ten structures be set up, with ten people sitting on each be placed. Whenever ten had eaten, ten others would come, and for each person of them, a Mudd of fresh dates was given.'

And I used to order for all the neighbors of the estate—the old man, the old woman, the child, the sick, the woman, and whoever was unable to come and eat from it—that for each person of them, a Mudd was given.

So when it was the picking time, I paid the workers, the supervisors, and the men their wages, and I carried the remainder to Medina. Then I distributed among the people of the houses and the deserving ones, the two camel loads, and the three, the less and the more, according to their deservingness. And after that, four hundred Dinars remained for me, while its gross produce had been four thousand Dinars.
ai.seo_question: How did Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) manage agricultural produce and distribute wealth to the community?
ai.summary: This hadith illustrates Imam al-Sadiq’s (peace be upon him) practical application of *ghalla* (agricultural produce) management, emphasizing communal welfare (*maslaha*) by ensuring open access for the public and targeted charity for the vulnerable. The narrative highlights the Shia principle of equitable distribution, where surplus is allocated based on merit (*istihqaq*) rather than mere ownership, reflecting a socio-economic model that balances productivity with social justice. This account serves as a foundational reference for Islamic jurisprudence regarding land management, worker wages, and the distribution of agricultural surplus in Shia legal tradition.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Idrees, and someone else, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Ali Bin Al Rayyan, from his father, from Yunus, or someone else, from the one who mentioned it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>!

It reached me that you<sup>asws</sup> did something regarding the produce of Ayn Ziyad, and I would love to hear it from you<sup>asws</sup>’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Yes. I<sup>asws</sup> used to order, whenever the fruits ripened, that a groove be grooved in its walls for the people to enter and eat; and I<sup>asws</sup> used to order, during every day, for ten structures (to be set up), with ten people being able to sit upon. Every time ten had eaten, ten others would come, attaching for every person of them, a Mudd (750 gms.) of dates.

And I<sup>asws</sup> used to order for the neighbours of the place, all of them, the old man, and the old woman, and the children, and the sick, and the women, and the one who was not able to come and eat from it, a Mudd (750 gms.) for each person of them.

So when it was the picking time, I fulfilled to the workers, and the allocated guards, and paid the workers to carry the remainder to Al-Medina. So I scattered it among the people of the houses and the deserving ones, the two camel loads, and the three, and the less and the more, upon a measurement of their deservedness, and there arrived to me after that, four hundred Dinars, and its gross produce had been four thousand Dinars’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ahmad ibn Idris and others has narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Ali ibn al-Rayyan from his father from Yunus or one other than him from those whom he has mentioned who has said the following:

“I once said to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, I have heard that you had done certain things about the produce of the farm in ‘Ayn Ziyad (name of a certain oasis) and I like to hear it from you.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, I would command at the time fruits ripened to open gaps in the walls so people could come in to eat. I would command every day to arrange ten platforms, on each of which ten people could sit. As soon as the ten finished eating, the other ten would come and every one received a handful (mud) a certain measurement, of dates.

I would command the neighbors of the property, every one of them, old man, old woman, children, people suffering from illness, women and those who were not able to come; everyone may eat one mud (a certain measurement).

When it was time to pick fruits I paid the guards, agents and men who were hired to carry what was left to al-Madinah. I distributed among the people of the houses and the deserving people two or three rahilah (camel-load) or less or more, proportionate to their deservingness. I earned four hundred dinar and its gross income was four thousand dinar.’”
